quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: What should you look for when choosing pants to wear while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Pants that do not fully cover your legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of leather.
questions.explanation: Wear long pants that cover your entire legs when riding. Leather offers the best protection. Your clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but loosely enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce your chances of having an accident?

options.text: Ride within one foot of the vehicle in front of you.
Signal only when you feel like it.
Stay alert and be ready to act to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to act to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure others can see you. Use your signals and brake light to communicate. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and next to you.

questions.question: What should you do when carrying a passenger?

options.text: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
Ride the same way you would without a passenger.
Make footrests available only for you, the driver.
Teach the passenger after you start riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must be equipped and adjusted to carry a passenger safely. It should have a large seat for two people and separate footrests for the passenger. You may need to adjust your headlight, tire pressure, and suspension for the extra weight.

questions.question: When does a motorcycle fit you properly?

options.text: When you can touch your feet to the ground while sitting.
When you can reach the controls by stretching.
When the handlebars go over your head.
When your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can touch your feet to the ground while sitting.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly if your feet can touch the ground while you are seated. You should be able to easily reach and operate the controls.

questions.question: What should you do with your feet when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Keep them firmly on the footrests.
Keep them away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep them firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Place your feet firmly on the footrests to maintain balance. Do not drag your feet or point your toes down, as your toes may catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can use them quickly if needed.

questions.question: When checking your tires before riding, what should you NOT check?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shininess
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear.

questions.question: What should you inspect before you ride?

options.text: The wear and tread of your tires

questions.correctAnswerText: The wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: What type of material should a protective jacket or pants be made of?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Wear a long jacket and long pants to cover your arms and legs while riding. Leather provides the best protection.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT required on a DOT-compliant helmet?

options.text: Bright colors painted on the outside

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap retention system.

questions.question: What should you do if you borrow a motorcycle?

options.text: Expect it to handle the same as your own bike.
Trust that the lender checked the brakes.
Leave extra space between you and other vehicles to allow more time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave extra space between you and other vehicles to allow more time to react.
questions.explanation: Check an unfamiliar motorcycle the same way you check your own. Ride cautiously and leave yourself extra space for stopping.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes at the same time to stop. They work best when used together.

questions.question: How often should you check your engine oil and transmission fluid levels?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle's engine oil and transmission fluid levels before each ride.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if you are experiencing:
questions.correctAnswerText: A wet riding surface.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when the road is wet or slippery. Your motorcycle will need more distance to stop safely.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When riding, a cushion of space helps you to:

options.text: Give you space to react to hazards.
Allow you to look at road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you space to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: Waiting one hour after one drink before riding:

options.text: Guarantees that you cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Guarantees that your riding skills will not be affected.
Should be fine as long as you ride slowly.
May not entirely remove alcohol effects from your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not entirely remove alcohol effects from your body.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour, but this varies by person. Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is typically located near the right handgrip.

questions.question: If wearing footwear with laces, the laces should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Be tucked in.
questions.explanation: Tuck in your shoelaces securely so they do not catch on your motorcycle while riding.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Stay where you are to avoid surprising the driver.
Wave at the other driver to get their attention.
Slow down until you are out of the blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down until you are out of the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a vehicle's blind spot, either speed up quickly or slow down and drop back to leave the spot safely.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
Only have one set of footrests.
Not encourage the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other motorists that a passenger is on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat large enough for two riders and footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear you wear.
